newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq bounds back, sets another record.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq bounds back, sets another record.

text.p: Nasdaq bounded back from Friday's sell-off and, led by Microsoft Corp and Intel Corp, set another record at the close.

"Things got overdone on Friday on the Greenspan remarks. When the Big Board came back today we followed it right up," said Robert Antolini, vice president in charge of OTC trading at Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette.
The Nasdaq Composite Index was up 28.6 points, or 2.2 percent, at 1316.3 while advances led declining issues by 2628 to 1782 on volume of about 589 million shares.
Stocks sold off on Friday following cautious remarks by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan roused fears that he would use interest rates as an instrument to quell the market's rise.

Microsoft was up 5-3/8 at 81-3/4, trading post-split. Microsoft said its Windows CE operating system for handheld computers will work on Intel architecture. The company said that it and Intel anticipate that they will be able to support development of products based on Windows CE and Intel processors by January 1997. Intel was up 4-7/16 at 130-1/8.
